main_issue: Whether strong-smelling cooking (e.g. D's fish curry) should be restricted or managed in the shared flat, and how (ban, ventilation, heads-up)

A-B.evidence: B agrees smell is a problem (T2) but proposes window opening (T8) and heads-up (T20) rather than A's restriction (T1, T11); A doesn't take up these ideas.

A-C.evidence: C complains of laundry smell (T3) and rejects the window idea (T9), which fits A's concern, but C never endorses a restriction or addresses A directly.

A-D.evidence: D resists: 'All cooking has a smell' (T6), 'So I should stop cooking my own food?' (T12); A insists 'we shouldn't be making smells that get on everything' (T17). D later concedes laundry has nowhere to go (T16, T24) but not the ban.

B-C.evidence: C rebuts B's window idea (T9), B's heads-up/laundry-in-rooms idea (T21, T23: 'It won't dry in my room'); B keeps proposing workarounds.

B-D.evidence: D rejects B's window idea ('She's right', T10 re C) and says there's nowhere for laundry (T24), undermining B's heads-up plan; D's stance isn't clearly pro or anti B's idea otherwise.

C-D.evidence: D backs C: 'She's right. The smell goes everywhere' (T10), 'Exactly' (T16), 'She's right. There's nowhere for wet laundry' (T24); though they differ on the ultimate cooking restriction.
